newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ says wd prefer 90-days at 8.5 pct, TWI 66.5.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ says wd prefer 90-days at 8.5 pct, TWI 66.5.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Tuesday that while its monetary policy statement assumes 90 day bank bills at 9.0 percent and the Trade-Weighted Index at 66.5, events since the MPS warranted somewhat easier conditions.
RBNZ governor Don Brash said a mix of "perhaps a combination of 90 day rates at 8.5 percent and TWI at 66.5" would be consistent with overall conditions.

"Having said that, and also in recognition of the uncertainties, the bank can accept monetary conditions which are either a little firmer than those represented by that level, or a little easier, as over the last few days."
Brash said the widening of the bank's inflation target to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent meant that its "aiming point" for inflation was now at 1.5 percent rather than 1.0 percent as previously.
But Brash said the bank would now have to be more vigilant about higher inflationary expectations.
"The new inflation target gives much less scope for an easing in conditions than might perhaps be assumed."
